papers.title: Characterization of bulk to thin wall mechanical response transition in powder bed AM
papers.abstract: Purpose In the development of powder bed additive manufacturing (AM) process parameters, the characterization of mechanical properties is generally performed through relatively large mechanical test samples that represent a bulk response. This provides an accurate representation of mechanical properties for equivalently sized or larger parts. However, as feature size is reduced, mechanical properties transition from a standard bulk response to a thin wall response where lower power border scans and surface roughness have a larger effect. Design/methodology/approach For this study, samples of wall thickness varying between 4.0 and 0.25 mm were built in 304L on the selective laser melting (SLM) platform and Ti-6Al-4V on the electron beam melting (EBM) platform. Samples were then mechanically tested, and fractography was performed for analysis. Findings This study experimentally identifies the threshold between bulk and thin wall mechanical properties for 304L SS on the SLM platform and Ti-6Al-4V on the EBM platform. A possible method for improving those properties and shifting the transition from bulk to thin wall response to smaller wall thicknesses by manipulation of scan pattern was investigated. Originality/value This study is a novel investigation into the effect of reduced wall thickness on the mechanical properties of a part produced by powder bed AM.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了增材制造中从块体到薄壁的力学性能转变，虽涉及Ti-6Al-4V但未关联植入物应力遮挡、多孔结构或疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address porous structures, stress shielding, fatigue behavior, or osseointegration, which are core to the biomedical AM direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究粉床增材制造中薄壁特征尺寸对力学性能的影响
summary_zh.method: 制备不同壁厚（0.25-4mm）的SLM 304L和EBM Ti-6Al-4V样品进行拉伸测试和断口分析
summary_zh.result: 识别出块体到薄壁力学性能转变的临界厚度，并发现扫描策略可改善薄壁性能
summary_zh.validation: 通过拉伸实验和断口形貌验证

summary_en.motivation: To characterize the transition from bulk to thin-wall mechanical response in powder bed additive manufactured parts as feature size decreases.
summary_en.method: Tensile tests and fractography were conducted on SLM 304L stainless steel and EBM Ti-6Al-4V samples with wall thicknesses ranging from 4.0 mm to 0.25 mm.
summary_en.result: The threshold thickness where mechanical properties shift from bulk to thin-wall behavior was identified, and scan pattern manipulation was shown to improve thin-wall properties.
summary_en.validation: Experimental mechanical testing and fractographic analysis confirmed the transition and effect of scan strategy.

papers.title: Applications of 3D bioprinting technology in regenerative medicine

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文综述了3D生物打印在再生医学中的应用，未涉及AI集成或实验验证，与用户研究方向的相关性较低。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a general review on bioprinting for regenerative medicine, lacking any AI integration, experimental validation, or autonomous decision-making specific to bioprinting workflows.

summary_en.motivation: This review aims to summarize the applications of 3D bioprinting technology in the field of regenerative medicine.
summary_en.method: A literature review approach was adopted to categorize and discuss various bioprinting applications.
summary_en.result: The paper presents a comprehensive overview of bioprinting for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine, including current challenges and future prospects.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation was performed; this is a review article.
